transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

For the last few months, I've been really overwhelmed because I feel like I'm constantly being watched and monitored by people. On top of that, I've had this intense energy for about six months where I barely sleep, and lately, I've started hearing voices that aren't there.
Have the voices or feeling watched ever continued for at least 2 weeks when you were not having that high-energy, little-sleep mood state? Or do they only happen during those mood episodes?

Yes, they definitely have. There was a period of about three weeks where my energy went back to normal and I was sleeping fine, but I was still hearing the voices and feeling like I was being watched. It was really confusing because my mood felt completely ordinary at the time.
Over the whole time you've been ill, have the high-energy mood episodes taken up most of the total time, or have the voices and feeling watched been present for longer than the mood episodes?

Yes, the high-energy periods have definitely taken up the majority of the time since I first got sick. Even though I still deal with the voices and feeling watched, those active, energetic episodes have been present for most of it.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type), Schizophrenia, Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features]. Based on this conversation, Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is now the leading and only current candidate because the patient reports psychotic symptoms persisting for about 3 weeks during a period of normal mood, which argues against Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features. The patient also reports that high-energy, decreased-sleep mood episodes have been present for the majority of the illness duration, which argues against Schizophrenia and supports schizoaffective disorder with bipolar-type mood episodes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a sustained manic syndrome with decreased need for sleep and intense energy lasting about six months, along with psychotic symptoms including auditory hallucinations and persecutory beliefs. Crucially, psychotic symptoms persisted for about three weeks during a period of normal mood and sleep, supporting schizoaffective disorder rather than a bipolar disorder with psychotic features. Mood episodes have also been present for the majority of the illness duration, consistent with the bipolar type specifier.
